# A tear-out Workspace without the WindowPosition addon fails silently

## Context

The operator's pre-release hand check (#14800, set on 2026-10-09 in [6089875583](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/14800#issuecomment-6089875583)) failed on 2026-10-11 ~18:40Z. In the installed Fleet Manager (Institution `4183eccd`, Engine `e8af9f3c3b`, Electron 43.5, macOS), he popped a pane out through its tab header's pop-out action and dragged the native popup by its title bar over the main app. No drop zones painted. In the Workstation the same journey paints them (the 13.2 film's native-return frame; `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL`). His rule from 10-10: a failed check is a small release blocker, likely a Dock enhancement.

## The Problem

A window moved by its native title bar is invisible to the page: no pointer events reach it. The engine learns where it is only through `Neo.main.addon.WindowPosition`, whose poll publishes `windowPositionChange` into `Neo.manager.Window`. `Workspace#observeWindowGeometry` arms that poll through an optional chain, `Neo.main?.addon?.WindowPosition?.setConfigs({observeMovement: true, observeResize: true, windowId})` (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:1428-1429`). An app that does not list the addon in `mainThreadAddons` gets a silent no-op. The manager's row for the vessel then stays its connect-time snapshot, every cross-window claim hit-tests a stale frame, and no drop zone answers.

The no-op is deliberate ("the app's opt-in is the addon itself", the #18077 spec), but nothing tells an app that turned tear-out on and forgot the opt-in. The Fleet Manager is that app: `apps/agentos/neo-config.json` lists `DockFlip, DragDrop, LocalStorage, Navigator, ResizeObserver, Stylesheet, WS/ShellPlane`, with `enableDockTearOutLifecycle: true`. The Workstation and the `crossWindow` example list `WindowPosition`. No Dock guide names the addon, so every 13.2 adopter of tear-out can fall into the same silent failure.

## The Architectural Reality

- Main-thread addon remotes are registered before the application loads: `Main.mjs` awaits each addon's `remotesReady()` before `WorkerManager.onWorkerConstructed`. Absence at Workspace construction therefore means the app does not list the addon; it is never a race.
- The precedent is #19449: a tear-out host whose `getDockProjectionOptions()` publishes no `crossWindowSortGroup` gets one warning per class, because a torn-out window could never return. This is the same failure one dependency lower.
- `observeWindowGeometry` is the documented override seam for "a realm that publishes geometry another way". The check belongs in its default body, so an override skips it.

## The Fix

*Re-scoped 2026-10-11 ~18:50Z on the operator's direction: main-thread addons load lazily (`Neo.currentWorker.getAddon(name, windowId)`, the dock's own Maximize plugin uses it for ResizeObserver), so the engine pulls the addon in itself instead of warning about a missing `neo-config.json` entry.*

1. `Workspace#observeWindowGeometry(windowId)` loads `WindowPosition` into **that window** through `getAddon`, then arms both observations. The load is per window, and that is the point: the Fleet Manager's vessel runs its own child app (`apps/agentos/childapps/widget/neo-config.json`: DocumentHead, DragDrop, Navigator, Stylesheet), so even a main-app config entry would not have reached it, and an armed call through another window's proxy reaches a realm without the addon.
2. Admitted vessels always load it (an admitted vessel is multi-window by definition). The host's own window loads it when the App Worker is a SharedWorker (`Neo.currentWorker.isSharedWorker`, the runtime fact, at the operator's direction): only such a worker serves several windows, so a dock in any other app (a dock layout without multi-window) loads nothing and starts no poll.
3. `DockLayoutsWindows.md`: the engine loads the addon on demand; no `mainThreadAddons` entry is needed for tear-out.
4. Unit arms in the #18077 describe: a tear-out host without the addon loads it for its own window; an admitted vessel loads it for the vessel's window; a plain host without it loads nothing.

The Fleet Manager needs no config change: it picks the fix up with its next engine pin move.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A tear-out Workspace whose app does not list `WindowPosition` arms movement and resize for its window through `getAddon('WindowPosition', windowId)`.
- [ ] AC-2 An admitted vessel arms its own window the same way, before the connection reaches an ownership branch.
- [ ] AC-3 A dock whose App Worker is not a SharedWorker loads nothing and starts no poll; in a SharedWorker app every dock host arms its window, whether or not the app lists the addon.
- [ ] AC-4 `DockLayoutsWindows.md` states that the engine loads the addon on demand.
- [ ] AC-5 The new arms fail on the old optional chain (red-first).

## Out of Scope

The Fleet Manager's pin move and reinstall, the Electron shell, and pointer-path drags.

## Related

#14800 (cut gate), #19449 (sibling warning), #18077 (geometry arming), #19539 (cross-window claim).
